# Incident Report — PCAP Forensic Analysis
**Evidence:** `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 packets, 2025-01-22 23:44:56 – 2025-01-23 00:38:18, SHA256 `e59db1c0…586`)
**Analyst tool:** tshark 4.x, static file carving via `--export-objects http`

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** |
| AD domain | BLUEMOONTUESDAY (bluemoontuesday.com), DC win-gsh54qlw48d.bluemoontuesday.com @ 10.1.17.2 |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString`, host also authenticates as `DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ$`) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Behavioral classification: PowerShell-based loader/backdoor that deploys a trojanized TeamViewer QuickSupport module for hands-on-keyboard remote access, consistent with the Matanbuchus loader-as-a-service TTP profile (fake-verification delivery, drive-serial bot ID, TeamViewer abuse via DLL sideload, shellcode injection via VirtualAlloc/CallWindowProcW).**

**Attribution basis: behavioral/TTP, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/YARA/hash-reputation lookup was performed (no internet access used, per instructions) — this conclusion is drawn purely from decoded script logic and dropped-file characteristics observed in the capture:

- Infection chain begins with visits to lure domains (`authenticatoor.org`, `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net`, `appointedtimeagriculture.com`) seconds before the first malicious download — consistent with a fake CAPTCHA/verification ("ClickFix"-style) lure that tricks the user into self-executing a command.
- An `<component><script language="VBScript">` stager launches hidden PowerShell that opens `azure.microsoft.com`/`teams.microsoft.com` as visual decoys while silently downloading the next stage.
- The PS loader computes a bot ID from the `C:` volume serial number (hex → Int64 = `1517096937`) and beacons `GET http://5.252.153.241/<botid>` every ~5 seconds in a loop, executing whatever is returned via `Invoke-Expression` — a classic PowerShell RAT/backdoor pattern.
- It drops a legitimate, signed TeamViewer GmbH `TeamViewer.exe` and `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll` alongside a 12 KB, version-info-stripped `TV.dll` (the normal TeamViewer TV.dll carries full version metadata; this one does not) — indicative of DLL sideloading to gain covert remote-hands-on-keyboard access under a trusted, signed process. Persistence is set via a Startup-folder `.lnk` to `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`.
- A later C2 command (`RunRH`) writes and reflectively loads shellcode (`VirtualAlloc` + `CallWindowProcW` trampoline) from `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1`, executed 4 separate times over the capture — evidence of live, interactive attacker command issuance, not a one-shot infection.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
| Indicator | Notes |
|---|---|
| `5.252.153.241:80` (HTTP) | Primary loader/C2 server. 594 request/response cycles from 23:45:56 to 00:38:18 (capture end, still active). |
| `185.188.32.26:443` (`master16.teamviewer.com`) | Legitimate TeamViewer DynGate relay contacted by the dropped/trojanized TeamViewer instance for attacker remote-control access. |

**Domains observed in the delivery chain**
- `authenticatoor.org` (→ 82.221.136.26)
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (→ 104.21.64.1, Cloudflare-fronted)
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (→ 217.70.186.109)
- `ds.reson8.com` (→ 104.18.8.76) — ad-tech domain queried in the same window, lower confidence as malicious infrastructure

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — initial VBScript stager
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — stage-2 PowerShell downloader
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — persistent beacon/backdoor loop script
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — dropped as `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — dropped as `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — dropped as `TV.dll` (anomalous/stripped sideload component)
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` — repeating C2 beacon/command-poll URL (bot ID = hex C: volume serial)

**Transferred files (SHA256)**
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| `264872` (VBScript stager) | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` |
| `29842.ps1` | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` |
| `pas.ps1` | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` |
| `TeamViewer.exe` | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` (genuine, signed TeamViewer GmbH binary — repurposed) |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll` | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` (genuine TeamViewer resource DLL) |
| `TV.dll` | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` (no version metadata, likely malicious sideload component) |

**Dropped-file paths / persistence** (from decoded PowerShell)
- `C:\ProgramData\huo\{TeamViewer.exe, Teamviewer_Resource_fr.dll, TV.dll, pas.ps1}`
- `%AppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\TeamViewer.lnk` → `C:\ProgramData\huo\TeamViewer.exe`
- `C:\ProgramData\jsLeow\skqllz.ps1` — shellcode reflective-loader written by the `RunRH` C2 command, executed 23:59:38, 00:25:09/11, 00:27:54 (four separate attacker commands during the capture)
